title: Data Processing Addendum for Research Collaboration — Publication & Use Annex (Draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This addendum ("Research Addendum") supplements the parties' existing Data Processing Agreement and governs processing activities relating to a research collaboration where Customer or Partner ("Research Partner") provides Redwood Inference ("Processor") data, or Redwood processes Customer data for joint research purposes. It focuses on publication rights, anonymization expectations, data minimization for model training, and obligations around human subjects/IRB compliance.

1. Definitions (selected and context-specific):
- Research Data: any Dataset provided for the research project, including text, logs, annotations, and derived features.
- Personal Data: as defined in the base DPA.
- Pseudonymized Data: data that has undergone irreversible pseudonymization techniques agreed in Appendix A.
- Re-identification Risk Assessment: an evaluation performed before publication or model release describing the residual risk a reasonable third party could re-identify data subjects.

2. Permitted Purposes and Processing Activities:
- Processor may process Research Data solely for the purposes set out in the Project Statement of Work (SOW) and as necessary for developing and evaluating models, reproducibility experiments, and drafting publications.
- Unless otherwise agreed in the SOW, Processor will not use Research Data for commercial productization unrelated to the collaborative research.
- Secondary use (new research questions or external sharing) requires written consent from Research Partner and a documented privacy review.

3. Publication and Authorship Protocols:
- Publication Review Period: The Research Partner has a 30-calendar-day review period prior to public release of papers, preprints, and technical reports that materially rely on Research Data. During this period the Research Partner may provide reasonable confidentiality requests limited to removing or redacting sensitive excerpts.
- Embargo Requests: The Research Partner may request an embargo (up to 90 days) for intellectual property or regulatory reasons; Processor will reasonably accommodate such requests. Extensions require mutual written agreement.
- Attribution: Authors will follow agreed attribution language in Appendix B, including acknowledgements of data sources and funding where applicable.

4. Data Minimization, De-identification, and Model Training Restrictions:
- Minimization: Project teams must document the minimal data fields required for each experiment. Any fields not necessary must be excluded prior to transfer.
- De-identification Baseline: Before any Research Data leaves Research Partner's controlled environment, it will be processed according to the de-identification checklist in Appendix A. For datasets containing sensitive identifiers, pseudonymization is required.
- Model Training Controls: Models trained with Research Data intended for public release must undergo a disclosure assessment (see Section 6). If the dataset contains any Special Category Personal Data, Processor will not release models or embeddings trained on that data without Research Partner consent and an approved mitigation plan.

5. Data Subject Rights and IRB/Legal Compliance:
- Controller Responsibilities: Where Research Partner is the Controller, it remains responsible for responding to Data Subject Access Requests (DSARs). Processor will assist within the timelines required by law and as set out in the base DPA.
- Human Subjects / IRB: Parties will each comply with applicable IRB or ethics board approvals. Processor will not commence human-subject processing activities until Research Partner confirms IRB clearance (or documented exemption).

6. Release Assessment and Re-identification Risk:
- Prior to public release of any Research Data, excerpts, or trained model artifacts, Processor will conduct a Re-identification Risk Assessment and produce a short report. Key elements: data provenance, anonymization steps taken, residual uniqueness metrics, and a recommended sensitivity label (public/internal/confidential).
- If the assessment indicates non-negligible re-identification risk, the parties will either (a) further de-identify the material, (b) redact high-risk examples from publications, or (c) limit distribution to an access-controlled repository.

7. Code and Model Artifact Handling:
- Code Repositories: Code that reproduces experiments may be published under an agreed license, but must not include datasets or secrets. Where scripts contain paths / small sample inputs, those samples must be sanitized.
- Model Weights and Embeddings: Publication of model weights or embeddings that were trained (wholly or in part) on Research Data requires a separate release approval. For models intended for public release, parties must agree on mitigation measures such as differential privacy parameters, filtered tokenizers, or output redaction.

8. Security Controls and Operational Measures:
- Minimum Controls: All Research Data transfers and storage will employ TLS in transit and encryption at rest. Access to raw Research Data is limited to the project team on a least-privilege basis.
- Logging and Monitoring: Processor will maintain access logs for Research Data for the duration of retention and will provide reasonable evidence of access controls upon request.
- Subprocessors: Processor may engage subprocessors but will disclose subprocessors relevant to the research project and accept audit obligations specific to Research Data processing.

9. Retention, Return, and Safe Disposal:
- Retention Schedule: Research Data will be retained only as long as necessary for the research project and archival reproducibility as described in the SOW. A default archival retention of 24 months post-project completion applies unless parties agree otherwise.
- Return/Destruction: Upon termination of the project or upon Research Partner request, Processor will return data where feasible or securely destroy all copies and provide a certificate of destruction.

10. Confidentiality, Publication Conflicts, and Dispute Escalation:
- Conflicts: If a conflict arises between the Processor's desire to publish and Research Partner confidentiality obligations (e.g., sponsor requirements), parties will negotiate in good faith, with escalation to the respective legal contacts listed in Appendix C.

11. Liability and Indemnity:
- Mutual liability will follow the base DPA. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, disputes arising specifically from willful disclosure of unredacted Personal Data in publications will be subject to fast-track remediation procedures in Appendix D.

12. Audit and Compliance:
- Audit Rights: Research Partner may request a one-time compliance audit specific to Research Data processing per project year; Processor will try to schedule within 60 days and produce redacted evidence where needed to protect other customers.

13. Amendments and Special Terms:
- Any modifications to this Addendum (e.g., extended embargoes, extended retention, release of models) must be recorded in a signed amendment or reflected in the Project SOW.

Appendices (summaries):
- Appendix A: De-identification checklist and pseudonymization techniques (hashing salted identifiers, date bucketing, removal of direct identifiers, scrubber rules for free text).
- Appendix B: Standard acknowledgement language and author affiliation rules.
- Appendix C: Legal & project contacts for escalation and publication clearance.
- Appendix D: Fast-track remediation procedure for accidental disclosure in publications.

Working notes / open items (internal use):
- Agree exact retention default (24 months is conservative; product/legal may prefer 12 months).
- Finalize pseudonymization routines and publish a small testing script in the research repo.
- Determine whether embargo length (90 days) should be dynamic per sponsor.
- Confirm the scope of audit artifacts Processor can provide without exposing other customers.

Sign-off
Draft prepared by: Aisha Patel (Security & Compliance).
Please route edits and comments through the Research collaboration channel (#research-collab) and link any paper drafts to the linked_artifacts list above.

Document classification: Draft internal template intended for use by research and legal teams when negotiating research DPAs or SOWs that involve publication or model release.
